akkas2019.evidence: Matches the Tiramisu compiler project that the thesis is about, but this is the official Tiramisu-Compiler org repo, not the thesis author's own implementation work.

baron:sm-thesis:2003.evidence: DynamoRIO is the tool platform used in the paper, but this is the official project repo created in 2014, a decade after the 2003 thesis; Iris Baron is not an author of this repo.

chen:pldi:2022.evidence: Benchmarks for auto-vectorization/revectorization match the paper's topic of SLP-based vectorization, though the repo predates the paper and ownership is unclear.

gottschlich:mapl:2018.evidence: Ithemal is a machine-learning-based instruction throughput estimator co-authored by Saman Amarasinghe's group, making it plausibly related to one of the paper's authors, but the paper itself is a position/survey paper on machine programming pillars and Ithemal is an independent tool, not the paper's own artifact.

ishibe:xsig:2026.evidence: NetBlocks is a prior PLDI 2024 work on custom network stacks that shares keyword overlap and co-author Brahmakshatriya, but this artifact repo belongs to a different paper and venue, not the xSIG 2026 paper being sought.

leger:meng-thesis:2004.evidence: DynamoRIO is the platform the thesis builds upon, but this repo is the official DynamoRIO project (created 2014, a decade after the 2004 thesis) and is not the thesis author's own implementation artifact.

petkov:meng-thesis:2001.evidence: StreamIt is the compiler infrastructure described in the thesis context (Darin Petkov's MEng work was part of the StreamIt project at MIT), but this repo belongs to a different author and is not specifically the unroll-and-squash implementation itself.
Mirror of the MIT StreamIt SVN repository; related infrastructure to the thesis topic but not authored by Darin Petkov and not the specific unroll-and-squash contribution.

ray:phd-thesis:2023.evidence: Python bindings for Finch.jl from the same research group, created around the same period, but is a companion tool rather than the core thesis contribution.

salsa.evidence: Lorenzo Di Tucci forked BWA (sequence aligner) which is directly related to the paper's topic of sequence alignment, suggesting it may have been used as a baseline or reference implementation, but it is not the paper's own artifact.

won:phd-thesis:2026.evidence: Fork of the TACO tensor algebra compiler from Jaeyeon Won's account, likely used as a dependency or baseline in the thesis, but it is a fork of prior work rather than the thesis's own contribution.

wong:meng-thesis:2004.evidence: Mirror of the MIT CSAIL StreamIt SVN repository, the platform underlying the thesis, but not authored by Jeremy Wong and only tangentially related as the broader project context.

zhao:cgo:2008.evidence: Name 'PIPA' and description about pipelined performance analytics loosely overlaps with the paper's topic, but this is a 2024 repo from a different institution with no direct tie to the 2008 CGO paper's authors (Zhao, Cutcutache, Wong).
